- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- bug-hunter: Universal, repo-agnostic Rust bug hunting framework. Finds silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, ordering/staleness bugs, crash-safety violations, and edge cases across any Rust codebase using Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning. (file: r11/bug-hunter/SKILL.md)
- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (file: r11/entire-search/SKILL.md)
- browser:control-in-app-browser: Control the in-app Browser for opening, navigating, inspecting visible or interactive page state, clicking, typing, screenshots, and local web testing. It can have existing signed-in sessions. For semantic operations on linked resources, prefer a purpose-built connector, API, or CLI when available. (file: r1/browser/26.831.20005/skills/control-in-app-browser/SKILL.md)
- courier:changeset: Classify verified changes and produce one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic. Use when the user asks to add a changeset, document a change, or determine release impact. (file: r6/changeset/SKILL.md)
- courier:commit: Prepare or create a conventional commit from staged work. Use when the user asks to commit changes or write a commit message; never create a commit without confirmation. (file: r6/commit/SKILL.md)
- courier:post-review: Deliver already-drafted PR comments or reviews. Use when the user asks to post a prepared reply, submit review comments, or resolve a named thread; never author or post content without confirmation. (file: r6/post-review/SKILL.md)
- courier:pr: Draft or open a reviewer-ready pull request from verified work. Use when the user asks to create a PR or write its description; require confirmation before any remote action. (file: r6/pr/SKILL.md)
- courier:receive-feedback: Assemble a neutral evidence package for incoming PR feedback. Use when the user asks to understand, triage, or respond to review comments on their own pull request. (file: r6/receive-feedback/SKILL.md)
- courier:release: Aggregate approved changesets into a release artifact. Use when the user asks to cut a release, calculate a version bump, or generate release notes from changesets. (file: r6/release/SKILL.md)
- mason:audit-plugin: Audit a plugin against the repository's concrete authoring and packaging rules. Use when the user asks whether a plugin conforms, is installable, or is ready to release. (file: r7/audit-plugin/SKILL.md)
- mason:design-schema: Design a versioned shared JSON Schema for an inter-agent handoff. Use when a workflow needs a durable producer-consumer contract or an existing contract must evolve. (file: r7/design-schema/SKILL.md)
- mason:evaluate: Evaluate a plugin workflow against a fixed hidden-oracle fixture. Use for release gates, regression checks, Claude/Codex comparisons, or longitudinal plugin analysis. (file: r7/evaluate/SKILL.md)
- mason:scaffold-plugin: Create a complete plugin skeleton for a new workflow. Use when the user asks to build or scaffold a plugin; derive structure from the repository constitution and validate the result before handoff. (file: r7/scaffold-plugin/SKILL.md)
- mason:scaffold-subagent: Add one conformant Claude-style agent prompt to an existing source plugin. Use when the user asks to add an agent without changing the plugin's unrelated routes. (file: r7/scaffold-subagent/SKILL.md)
- muse:component: Turn UI intent into an implementation-ready component specification. Use when the user asks to specify, audit, or gate a component design before planning or implementation. (file: r8/muse/1.0.1/skills/component/SKILL.md)
- navigator:plan: Turn an approved persisted specification into an executable implementation plan, amend a plan after a spec correction, estimate a plan, or adversarially challenge one. Use for “write a plan”, “break this spec into tasks”, “estimate this plan”, or “challenge this plan”. (file: r8/navigator/2.3.2/skills/plan/SKILL.md)
- plugin-management:plugin-management: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access. (file: r3/plugin-management/0.1.0/skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md)
- presentations:Presentations: Read, create or edit PowerPoint or Google Slides decks. Use for presentation, slide deck, PowerPoint, PPT, PPTX, or Google Slides requests. (file: r4/presentations/26.905.11957/skills/presentations/SKILL.md)
- ranger:audit: Find evidence-backed reachable defects in Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Use for bug hunts, security audits, suspected defects, or post-remediation verification; do not use for general code explanation. (file: r8/ranger/3.2.2/skills/audit/SKILL.md)
- scribe:architect: Specify a structural correction when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` reveals a recurring defect class, missing domain model, or architectural gap. (file: r9/architect/SKILL.md)
- scribe:audit-architecture: Check a spec against a persisted workspace architecture model, or build or refresh that model. Use for “does this fit the architecture?”, “audit against the arch model”, or “map this codebase architecture”. (file: r9/audit-architecture/SKILL.md)
- scribe:audit-spec: Adversarially review a spec for ambiguity, untestable criteria, missing error behavior, and scope defects. Use for “audit this spec”, “is this spec complete?”, or before gate-spec. (file: r9/audit-spec/SKILL.md)
- scribe:correct-spec: Correct a persisted specification when implementation evidence proves a criterion contradicts the live system. Use after a `spec_contradiction`, not for ordinary implementation difficulty. (file: r9/correct-spec/SKILL.md)
- scribe:draft-spec: Draft a testable specification from a requirement and optional research evidence. Use for “draft a spec”, “spec this out”, or “write a spec for this requirement”. (file: r9/draft-spec/SKILL.md)
- scribe:gate-spec: Issue the binding pass or fail decision for a specification before planning begins. Use for “gate this spec”, “is this ready to plan?”, or “check this spec before implementation”. (file: r9/gate-spec/SKILL.md)
- scribe:spec-drift: Compare a persisted specification with current implementation and tests to find covered, uncovered, and drifted criteria. Use for “check spec drift” or “does the code still match this spec?”. (file: r9/spec-drift/SKILL.md)
- scribe:verify-spec: Verify that each draft specification criterion is grounded in its requirement and research evidence. Use for “does this match the requirement?”, “is this grounded?”, or before an audit or gate. (file: r9/verify-spec/SKILL.md)
- sentinel:gate: Independently verify an artifact against its criteria before it crosses a lifecycle boundary. Use for requirements, specs, plans, implementations, PRs, and explicit readiness checks. (file: r8/sentinel/2.1.2/skills/gate/SKILL.md)
- sites:sites-building: Use Sites to build websites, including landing pages, portfolios, dashboards, portals, trackers, hubs, and internal tools. Always use Sites when the project contains `.openai/hosting.json`. (file: r2/sites-building/SKILL.md)
- sites:sites-hosting: Host websites with Sites. Always use after `sites-building`, and use for website publishing, deployment, hosting management, or projects containing `.openai/hosting.json`. (file: r2/sites-hosting/SKILL.md)
- smith:implement: Execute an approved plan or specification with targeted implementation, tests, evidence, review, and independent verification. Use for “implement this”, “execute the plan”, “build this feature”, “write the code”, or “refactor without changing behavior”. (file: r8/smith/2.4.2/skills/implement/SKILL.md)
- spreadsheets:Spreadsheets: Use skill when user requests to create, modify, analyze, visualize, or work with spreadsheet files (`.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.csv`, `.tsv`) or Google Sheets with formulas, formatting, charts, tables, and recalculation. Do not use for live controlling Microsoft Excel app or a live Excel session. (file: r5/spreadsheets/SKILL.md)
- spreadsheets:excel-live-control: Control an open or active Microsoft Excel workbook through the ChatGPT add-in or connected session. Use when the user tags the Microsoft Excel app in Codex or follows up on an established live Excel task. Do not use for standalone spreadsheet files or Google Sheets. (file: r5/excel-live-control/SKILL.md)
- template-creator:template-creator: Create or update a reusable personal Codex artifact-template skill. Use when the user invokes $template-creator or asks in natural language to create a reusable template from a reference document, presentation, spreadsheet, Google Docs, Slides, or Sheets link, ImageGen or Product Design image, email, Slack message, or Site project, or explicitly asks to edit or update a passed artifact-template skill. Do not use for one-off creation from an existing template. (file: r4/template-creator/26.905.11957/skills/template-creator/SKILL.md)
- vanguard:research: Investigate a technical or product question before committing to a design. Use for “research this”, “what are the options?”, “what does the codebase do?”, “is there a way to…?”, or “what are the risks?”. (file: r8/vanguard/2.0.2/skills/research/SKILL.md)
- visualize:visualize: Create visualizations and interactive tools directly in conversation. Proactively use to show how something works; explore 'what happens when', 'what changes', or 'help me understand'; compare or inspect; create simulations, maps, charts, graphs, and mockups. Use standard tools for static scientific figures. (file: r1/visualize/1.0.27/skills/visualize/SKILL.md)
- weaver:audit-backlog: Audit the health of a backlog of open requirements against specifications, plans, and implemented evidence. Use for “audit the backlog”, “what is missing coverage?”, or “what should we clean up?”. (file: r10/audit-backlog/SKILL.md)
- weaver:capture-need: Turn a raw product need, issue, or user complaint into a traceable requirement draft without inventing missing facts. Use when the user says “we need…”, “users are asking…”, or asks to capture a need before writing a spec. (file: r10/capture-need/SKILL.md)
- weaver:clarify-requirement: Find and close the single highest-value gap in a requirement draft. Use when a requirement needs to be ready for specification, or the user asks what is missing from it. (file: r10/clarify-requirement/SKILL.md)
- weaver:connect-requirement: Check whether one requirement overlaps existing requirements, specifications, plans, or implementation. Use for “is this already captured?”, “does this overlap?”, or “what does this relate to?”. (file: r10/connect-requirement/SKILL.md)
- weaver:prioritize-backlog: Rank a set of requirements into an actionable order using impact, urgency, dependencies, and evidence. Use for “what should we do first?”, “rank the backlog”, or “what is most urgent?”. (file: r10/prioritize-backlog/SKILL.md)

{
  "id": "T1",
  "title": "Stage nonbreaking exact-observation evidence and receipt construction",
  "steps": [
    "After product PM-002 has staged private successor identities, add ReleaseObservationEvidence and pure complete-observation receipt construction/validation helpers beside the existing receipt implementation in model release.rs. Use the product-owned successor identity contract; do not replace product operation/slot schemas or add a compatibility decoder.",
    "Require canonical operation ordering, exact intent-digest and operation-roster binding, role-matched safe identity/digest/byte-length evidence, and newly-produced versus already-present provenance; reject endpoints, credentials, headers, provider stderr, arbitrary strings, and mutable configuration from durable evidence.",
    "Keep the public ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state signature untouched during this additive task so its existing unit consumers still compile. Stage the replacement constructor's exact-roster rules without making it a second accepted production wire format; T4 owns removal of the old constructor and the atomic migration of every caller. The journal is never used as exact evidence.",
    "Add model tests for unknown fields, duplicate or missing operation entries, non-canonical ordering, mismatched evidence identity, mismatched intent digest, unsafe evidence, and canonical round-trip of complete exact receipts containing both provenance outcomes.",
    "Run rtk just fmt-check, rtk just lint and rtk just test; expect the existing workspace and staged pure receipt tests to pass without a broken production signature."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T2",
  "title": "Expose canonical remote annotated-tag observation and confirmation",
  "steps": [
    "Extend GitDataSource with the remote annotated-tag read and push-confirmation operations required by the gated convergence contract, carrying configured remote identity, tag name, target commit, and annotation digest. Add all required trait methods together with GitRepository, ShellGit and GitAccess implementations and affected tests in this same compiling task; no required method is committed without every implementation.",
    "Implement the contract in GitRepository, ShellGit, and GitAccess so native/shell selection preserves typed absent, exact, conflict, and VCS failure semantics; retain local tag creation through existing GitAccess and remove no caller yet.",
    "Add temporary-bare-remote tests for absent, exact annotated tag, target conflict, annotation conflict, a local-only matching tag, successful push followed by exact remote readback, and command failure.",
    "Run rtk just fmt-check, rtk just lint and rtk just test; expect a local-only tag never to count as exact and remote conflict or transport failure to remain distinguishable."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T3",
  "title": "Consume the product artifact capability and implement one provider observer",
  "steps": [
    "Within CUTOVER-1 consume product PM-005's ValidatedArtifactManifest and existing verify_artifact_manifest constructor unchanged. The observer gets expected slots/bytes only through that capability, bound to the same ValidatedReleaseIntent; do not redefine slots, DAG/prepared variants, raw-manifest validation or CLI artifact input signatures.",
    "Implement the gated closed graph-only OperationObservation and ExternalConflict taxonomy plus observe_prepared in release_observation.rs; dispatch exhaustively over every graph-private prepared operation and convert only exact proof to model ReleaseObservationEvidence. The private prepared variants and their canonical map were fully defined by PM-004. Keep the observer implementation in release_observation.rs and migrate every sibling pre/post/execute/reconcile observation to it during T4; delete old local-only/boolean observers from release.rs in this same boundary.",
    "Implement registry artifact observation against SPEC-001's validated manifest: crates.io-compatible checksum, npm packed tarball integrity or bytes, and PyPI named distribution SHA-256; classify exact subsets with only verified missing work as Incomplete and classify different or unprovable bytes as Conflict or Unverifiable.",
    "Use task T2 GitAccess/GitDataSource remote operations for tag observation and post-push confirmation instead of release.rs local rev-parse/for-each-ref logic.",
    "Use supported gh API arguments for GitHub Release and asset observation; classify real nonzero 404 as Absent, preserve 401/403/429/5xx/timeout/malformed output as Unverifiable, use separately verified remote-tag identity rather than target_commitish, and distinguish ForgePrepare draft/published-successor exactness from ForgePublish asset-roster completion.",
    "Add focused CommandRunner tests for all observation outcomes, registry exact/incomplete/conflict/unverifiable values, supported gh argv, nonzero 404, and GitHub Release/asset exactness rules.",
    "No standalone passing-check claim within CUTOVER-1: finish T3-DISPATCH -> T4 -> T5 and run the joint workspace runner gate. Focused tests named here become mandatory parts of that gate."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T3-DISPATCH",
  "title": "Publish the exact prevalidated registry and forge artifact bytes",
  "steps": [
    "Baseline: release.rs::dispatch_registry invokes cargo_publish_argv with a source Cargo.toml, npm_publish_argv selects npm/pnpm/yarn/bun workspace packaging, and pypi_publish_argv builds into dist/ then uploads a glob with --skip-existing. None binds the outgoing bytes. Replace ALL those durable provider dispatch callers and shared argv builders here; product PM-004 continues to own only prepared identities/DAG.",
    "Require dispatch_prepared to receive the same ValidatedReleaseIntent plus ValidatedArtifactManifest and a verified missing-work set from T3. Before each irreversible command, call PM-005's shared snapshot/accessor to compare SHA-256 and byte length again, retain exactly that verified buffer or private immutable staging file, and submit only those bytes. File drift, intent/slot mismatch, or unprovable regeneration fails before any publish/upload request; post-effect comparison alone cannot satisfy this gate.",
    "Choose direct crates.io-compatible artifact upload for Cargo: add registry_artifacts.rs to construct a PUT /api/v1/crates/new request consisting of little-endian u32 metadata length, JSON package metadata, little-endian u32 .crate length and the already validated .crate byte buffer. Derive metadata from the validated archive and exact prepared package inputs. registry_argv.rs builds the fixed transport command and existing CommandRunner::run_with_stdin submits that body; resolve API routing only from the prepared registry binding. Remove cargo publish --manifest-path repackaging entirely. Before request submission validate embedded .crate digest and safe lengths; preserve registry error handling, including error objects returned with HTTP 200. Add bounded gzip/tar reading dependencies through the workspace and graph Cargo manifests using toml_edit, updating Cargo.lock via project runners; parse without extracting unsafe archive paths. The transport is curl PUT with --data-binary @- and finite timeout, fed the verified fixed request body. Keep credentials in a private request-header file rather than argv/output and redact failures; an unsupported stdin-capable runner fails before submission. Test the real CLI stdin runner against a local HTTP sink.",
    "Unify npm, pnpm, yarn and bun workspace publication behind npm publish <private-validated-tarball-path> --ignore-scripts with the prepared registry, access and dist-tag arguments. Those managers may produce artifacts in the credential-free build stage; release dispatch never runs a workspace publish or pack command. Change registry_argv.rs signatures to take the exact validated tarball handle/path and migrate all manager match arms/callers and their argv tests in this same task. Validate tool support before mutation and fail explicitly if the canonical tarball publisher is unavailable.",
    "For PyPI make each RegistryArtifactPublish slot one exact named wheel or sdist. Replace pypi_publish_argv's build+glob sequence with one twine upload of the private validated file for that slot; no python -m build, wildcard or --skip-existing in execute. Observe every expected distribution first, report exact files and upload only the closed missing subset; a wrong digest or unexpected conflicting filename prevents mutation.",
    "Implement ProductTag mutation via T2's canonical remote push/readback, ForgePrepare draft creation, per-slot ArtifactUpload and final ForgePublish against T3's observed state. Asset uploads consume the same exact snapshot capability, never overwrite a same-name conflict and never publish a draft before all six required assets and provenance are exact.",
    "Add argv-sensitive and local-HTTP body-capture tests for Cargo embedded .crate bytes, npm/pnpm/yarn/bun use of the same exact tarball publisher, and single-file PyPI partial-resume. Mutate the source package, staged artifact and any attempted regenerated package separately; assert changed artifact/outgoing digest yields zero irreversible requests, while source edits cannot make a provider command repackage. Assert the received payload digest equals the prevalidated manifest for every provider, and that stale extra dist files are never uploaded. Cover u32 length overflow, malformed archive metadata, credential redaction and HTTP 200 with a registry errors object; none may become a receipt.",
    "Inventory all cargo_publish_argv/npm_publish_argv/pypi_publish_argv callers and structurally similar publish subprocess paths with rg; remove old regenerating siblings rather than keeping an escape route. Update release.rs, registry_argv.rs, publish_tests and all helper tests in this same CUTOVER-1 boundary. T4/T5 finish executor and CLI consumers of dispatch_prepared's new signature before verification.",
    "Run rtk just fmt-check, rtk just lint, rtk just test and rtk just wasm-check only after T5 completes the joint cutover. The registry_argv unit tests, registry_artifacts body-capture tests and publish_tests integration target must all execute and pass."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T4",
  "title": "Converge execution from observations and atomically persist receipts",
  "steps": [
    "Within CUTOVER-1 promote T1's strict exact-observation receipt as the sole production schema and remove ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state plus every state-only completion test/caller in model release.rs. Migrate any receipt exports and state/receipt store consumers in the same boundary; product contract types remain PM-004-owned.",
    "Replace Pending-only reconcile_release_execution with the gated complete canonical-DAG observation report that invokes task T3's observer exactly once per operation, requires no ApplyPermit, and does not reach any mutation route.",
    "Replace execute_release and execute_release_with_artifacts with converge_release over the product-owned validated artifact capability: observe prerequisites and operations in canonical order regardless of saved Pending, Attempting, Published, AlreadySatisfied, Failed or Blocked; invoke T3-DISPATCH only for Absent or verified missing work of Incomplete at most once per invocation, then re-observe as Exact. Update release.rs dispatch calls, graph exports and CLI commands/release.rs graph invocation signatures atomically here; T5 completes typed output handling before the batch can pass.",
    "Persist state transitions atomically through ReleaseStateStore only as intent-bound diagnostics; missing, stale, unreadable, or lost state must neither widen authority nor prevent fresh observation recovery.",
    "Add explicit-path ReleaseReceiptStore as the sole production writer, backed by callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write, and persist/return a receipt only after one final complete exact observation pass. Do not read a receipt as proof on a later run.",
    "Add tests for recovery from Attempting, Failed, Blocked, and absent journal states; non-exact prerequisite gating; one-attempt-per-invocation behavior; final-pass completeness; atomic state/receipt write failure; and structurally read-only reconciliation.",
    "Do not run a claimed passing workspace gate with old CLI return consumers: finish T5 in the same CUTOVER-1 compilation/commit boundary, then execute the joint repository runner checks. All model receipt, graph executor/store and CLI immediate-consumer tests must pass together."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T5",
  "title": "Expose convergence and complete reconciliation through the CLI",
  "steps": [
    "Finish CUTOVER-1 by migrating every CLI caller/result consumer of T4's graph signatures in commands/release.rs, cli.rs, error.rs and durable/dry-run tests. Use PM-005's input validation capability unchanged, route execute to converge_release returning the persisted receipt, and route reconcile to the complete observation report. No old executor result or raw artifact manifest can cross this call boundary.",
    "Route reconcile to the complete graph observation report, render all operation observations in JSON and text, and make every absent, incomplete, conflict, unverifiable, pending, attempting, failed, blocked, missing receipt, or receipt-write failure a nonzero exit with operation identity and recovery action.",
    "Add CLI tests proving successful execute renders a persisted receipt, JSON retains complete typed observations, incomplete reconciliation exits nonzero, and reconcile cannot obtain a permit or reach registry publish, Git push, GitHub creation, or upload routes.",
    "Run rtk just fmt-check, rtk just lint, rtk just test and rtk just wasm-check. Expected: the entire model/graph/CLI successor cutover compiles and all relevant tests pass, including durable_release_e2e_tests and dry_run_invariant_tests. Only now create the joint CUTOVER-1 commit; do not separately commit broken model, executor, artifact-constructor or CLI signatures."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T5-FAILPOINT",
  "title": "Expose rehearsal-only interruption failpoints at real executor boundaries",
  "steps": [
    "Add a closed graph-private ReleaseFailpoint enum for every post-provider-mutation/pre-following-journal-or-receipt boundary, plus terminal-state and receipt persistence boundaries. Inject it through an executor control seam whose default is disabled and which cannot change operation identity, provider input, observation classification or receipt contents.",
    "Expose `--rehearsal-failpoint <name>` only on release execute. Graph must reject it unless the validated immutable intent carries PM-004's rehearsal destination binding; production destination, absent binding, unknown name and reconcile all fail before credentials or provider mutation.",
    "At the selected real boundary, terminate with a stable intentional-interruption diagnostic after the provider effect but before the named following persistence step. Do not synthesize provider results, mark success, write a receipt, retain an in-memory continuation token or log credentials.",
    "Add process-level tests for every failpoint name, rejection on production intent, one-and-only-one trigger, and fresh-process resume using external observation with and without the prior journal.",
    "Run rtk just fmt-check, rtk just lint and rtk just test; expect the disabled path to remain behavior-identical and every rehearsal failpoint to produce a nonzero intentional interruption."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "T6",
  "title": "Exercise realistic provider and interruption-resume convergence boundaries",
  "steps": [
    "Build real temporary bare-Git-remote cases for absent, exact, conflicting, and local-only tags, then assert fresh-runner execution reads the remote and does not duplicate an exact effect.",
    "Use argv-sensitive gh fixtures matching installed gh parsing and model real nonzero 404 plus 401, 403, 429, and 5xx responses; assert absence is distinct from unverifiable failure and an exit-zero-only or argv-insensitive fake cannot satisfy the tests.",
    "Use local HTTP registry fixtures for absent, exact, conflicting and unverifiable metadata, with captured upload bodies proving outgoing .crate, npm/pnpm/yarn/bun tarball, wheel and sdist hashes match the validated entries. Test source/package regeneration drift and artifact drift before mutation with request counters equal to zero; test PyPI exact-wheel/missing-sdist and inverse cases upload only the named missing file.",
    "Drive T5-FAILPOINT at attempt persistence, every independently uploadable artifact, provider success, post-effect observation, terminal-state persistence, and receipt persistence; resume once with the journal and once without it in a fresh CLI process.",
    "Assert every resume either produces only verified missing work and the same complete receipt or exits nonzero for conflict/unverifiable input; assert no scenario returns a successful incomplete state.",
    "Run rtk just fmt-check, rtk just lint and rtk just test; expect all real-contract and interruption-resume boundary cases to pass.",
    "Name and run the real new integration targets release_convergence_boundary_tests and release_convergence_e2e_tests through rtk just test; current argv unit tests reside in registry_argv.rs and must remain enabled. Record coverage for every successor operation variant for product PM-006's final no-orphan architecture assertion."
  ]
}

docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002.json:79:      "criterion": "Graph returns a complete typed observation report and receipt only after every intended operation is observed Exact in the same final pass and a matching receipt is atomically persisted. callisto-cli maps any Pending, Attempting, Failed, Blocked, Absent, Incomplete, Conflict, Unverifiable, missing operation, missing receipt, or receipt-write failure to nonzero exit and renders the incomplete operation and recovery action in text and complete JSON.",
docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002.json:109:      "criterion": "Graph reconciliation is structurally read-only and returns a complete typed report for every operation, not merely a list of locally eligible Pending entries. It requires no ApplyPermit and invokes no registry publish, Git push, GitHub creation, or upload route. callisto-cli preserves the full report in JSON and exits nonzero when the intended release is not completely Exact.",
docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002.json:119:      "criterion": "Interruption tests stop at each boundary between attempt persistence, each independently uploadable provider artifact, provider success, post-effect observation, terminal-state persistence, and receipt persistence, then resume with both the same journal and no journal on a fresh runner. Every case either uploads only verified missing work and converges without repeating an Exact effect or exits nonzero for Conflict/Unverifiable; no case can return successful incomplete state.",
docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002.json:131:  "revision_note": "Corrects the local-only, no-automatic-retry recovery semantics in the draft .claude release execution specifications. External state is authoritative for convergence; the journal is not.",

# Print an optspec for argparse to handle cmd's options that are independent of any subcommand.
function __fish_callisto_global_optspecs
    string join \n format= cwd= dry-run h/help V/version
end

function __fish_callisto_needs_command
    # Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
    set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
    set -e cmd[1]
    argparse -s (__fish_callisto_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
    or return
    if set -q argv[1]
        # Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
        echo $argv[1]
        return 1
    end
    return 0
end

function __fish_callisto_using_subcommand
    set -l cmd (__fish_callisto_needs_command)
    test -z "$cmd"
    and return 1
    contains -- $cmd[1] $argv
end

            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --emit-decision)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --format)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "text json" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --cwd)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                *)
                    COMPREPLY=()
                    ;;
            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

# Print an optspec for argparse to handle cmd's options that are independent of any subcommand.
function __fish_callisto_global_optspecs
    string join \n format= cwd= dry-run h/help V/version
end

function __fish_callisto_needs_command
    # Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
    set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
    set -e cmd[1]
    argparse -s (__fish_callisto_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
    or return
    if set -q argv[1]
        # Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
        echo $argv[1]
        return 1
    end
    return 0
end

function __fish_callisto_using_subcommand
    set -l cmd (__fish_callisto_needs_command)
    test -z "$cmd"
    and return 1
    contains -- $cmd[1] $argv
end

use builtin;
use str;

set edit:completion:arg-completer[callisto] = {|@words|
    fn spaces {|n|
        builtin:repeat $n ' ' | str:join ''
    }
    fn cand {|text desc|
        edit:complex-candidate $text &display=$text' '(spaces (- 14 (wcswidth $text)))$desc
    }
    var command = 'callisto'
    for word $words[1..-1] {
        if (str:has-prefix $word '-') {
            break
        }
        set command = $command';'$word
    }
    var completions = [
        &'callisto'= {
            cand --format 'Output format for command results'
            cand --cwd 'Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory)'
            cand --dry-run 'Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk'
            cand -h 'Print help'
            cand --help 'Print help'
            cand -V 'Print version'
            cand --version 'Print version'
            cand add 'Create a new changeset describing pending package changes'
            cand status 'Show the workspace''s pending changesets and diagnostics'
            cand matrix 'Print the workspace''s native-build target matrix as JSON or a table'
            cand version 'Consume pending changesets and bump package versions accordingly'
            cand pre 'Manage prerelease mode for the workspace'
            cand validate 'Check that changesets and the dependency graph are well-formed'
            cand snapshot 'Apply a temporary, non-persistent version bump for a snapshot release'
            cand init 'Scaffold Callisto configuration in the current workspace'
            cand plan-publish 'Compute which packages are ready to publish and print the publish plan'
            cand publish 'Publish ready packages to their ecosystem registries via native CLI tools'
            cand compose-pr-body 'Generate a pull request body summarizing pending release changes'
            cand tag 'Create git tags for packages in a publish plan'
            cand filter-plan 'Filter a publish plan down to what a publish report confirms actually succeeded, dropping anything that failed'
            cand release 'Create, inspect, reconcile, or execute durable release intents'
            cand release-pr 'Decide the next managed release-pull-request operation from a forge snapshot'
            cand completions 'Generate shell completion scripts'
            cand schema 'Print the JSON schema for a report type'
            cand help 'Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)'
        }
        &'callisto;add'= {

# Print an optspec for argparse to handle cmd's options that are independent of any subcommand.
function __fish_callisto_global_optspecs
    string join \n format= cwd= dry-run h/help V/version
end

function __fish_callisto_needs_command
    # Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
    set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
    set -e cmd[1]
    argparse -s (__fish_callisto_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
    or return
    if set -q argv[1]
        # Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
        echo $argv[1]
        return 1
    end
    return 0
end

function __fish_callisto_using_subcommand
    set -l cmd (__fish_callisto_needs_command)
    test -z "$cmd"
    and return 1
    contains -- $cmd[1] $argv
end

# Print an optspec for argparse to handle cmd's options that are independent of any subcommand.
function __fish_callisto_global_optspecs
    string join \n format= cwd= dry-run h/help V/version
end

function __fish_callisto_needs_command
    # Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
    set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
    set -e cmd[1]
    argparse -s (__fish_callisto_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
    or return
    if set -q argv[1]
        # Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
        echo $argv[1]
        return 1
    end
    return 0
end

function __fish_callisto_using_subcommand
    set -l cmd (__fish_callisto_needs_command)
    test -z "$cmd"
    and return 1
    contains -- $cmd[1] $argv
end
